page.overview:
What is Mearas?

The Mearas were a breed of wild horses in the north of Middle-earth. According to lore, the ancestors of the Mearas were brought from the West by Oromë, whose steed Nahar could be the sire of the breed.

They surpass normal horses in intelligence, speed and strength. Taking Shadowfax as an example, Mearas was generally grey/silver stallions, and they could understand the speech of Men.

They were descended from Felaróf, who was tamed by the first King of Rohan, Eorl. The descendants of Felaróf would later become the mounts of the King of Rohan, and would bear no one except for the Kings of the Mark and their sons.

During the Third Age, Gandalf was given consent to ride Shadowfax, Lord of the Mearas. Shadowfax continued to accompany Gandalf throughout the latter half of the War of the Ring. He was also present at the Grey Havens when Gandalf sailed to Valinor.
